findingsBeforeBuild.finding: Card snapshot says lines 153, 173 and 509 stamp the legacy pair on every cad-parcel-roll, identity.alias and flood atom. At 26e0c04: 153 = cad-parcel-roll (pipelineFromRows), 173 = identity.alias (pipelineFromRows), 509 = the rate-probe synthetic atoms (syntheticStagedAtoms), NOT flood. Flood atoms come from src/stages/demote/flood.mjs floodAtomsToStage line 151, which already stamps mapAccessPolicy(public-free) = the contract's three-field canonical form. Consequence: flood atoms in the store are not expected to carry the legacy pair; the re-stamp still scans every entity type for the county so nothing is assumed. Second mechanism considered: an earlier flood writer stamped legacy pairs before flood.mjs took mapAccessPolicy; not verifiable without the store (reads forbidden by the dispatch), so the job matches on the pair, never on entity type.

src/lib/six-field.mjs normalizeAccess is used only by sixFieldCandidate (adapter candidates, the production side); nothing in six-field classifies stored rows. The card's clause 'keeps reading the legacy pairs only where it classifies stored rows' therefore leaves nothing for six-field to keep: sixFieldCandidate will refuse a legacy pair (ACCESS_NOT_CANONICAL) instead of silently translating it, and the declared legacy table plus a stored-row classifier move to one module src/lib/access-pair.mjs, used by the re-stamp job.

Atom identity does not include access: atomId = contentId({entityType, nodeId, claim, logicVersion}) (src/stages/write/index.mjs:18). The stamp change therefore keeps every atom_did stable, the re-stamp is an in-place UPDATE, and a future writer re-run ON CONFLICT DO UPDATEs the same did with a canonical body. LOGIC_VERSION is NOT bumped; bumping it would mint new dids beside the old rows and duplicate the county.

mergeFromFactoryStage without stagedSince merges every write_stage_atoms row for (entityType, county); accessPolicyProjection currently maps a legacy body onto the column, so a stale legacy body in the Factory staging half could re-enter the atoms store through a whole-stage merge after the re-stamp. Today no live path does that for cad-parcel-roll (the chunk path passes stagedSince; the flood path merges flood-* types, which are canonical), but the path exists. accessPolicyProjection will refuse a legacy pair with ACCESS_NOT_CANONICAL so the stale staging half is inert until re-staged by a writer run.

The Dockerfile copies only src/ and migrations/ into the image; a file at jobs/restamp-access.mjs would not ship. The job lands at src/jobs/restamp-access.mjs and is wired through src/cli.mjs like every other job (the card's jobs/restamp-access.mjs is read as the repo's src/jobs/ convention).

src/control/reaper.mjs COMMAND_JOBS / PHASE_JOBS give each run an execution affinity; a restamp run without an entry would be matchable to any factory execution by start time. Both tables gain restamp-access -> factory-restamp-access, with a test.

Template execution pattern (A-019): factory-conformant's template args are the bare command and the loop passes container-override args per county. factory-restamp-access will be deployed with --args=restamp-access (which alone refuses COUNTY_REQUIRED, so the template cannot succeed by accident) and executed with --args=restamp-access,--county=<fips>,--dry-run then ...,--apply.

design.accessPairModule: src/lib/access-pair.mjs: PUBLIC_RECORD_ACCESS = frozen {catalog-listed, anyone-free}; ACCESS_NOT_CANONICAL; LEGACY_ACCESS_PAIRS = frozen { public/anonymous: {discoverability: catalog-listed, entitlement: anyone-free, accessPolicy: public-free} } mirroring LDT PR #519 exactly; legacyPairKey(access); classifyStoredAccess(access) -> {kind: canonical|legacy|unknown, key, canonical}; assertCanonicalAccessPair(access) refuses a legacy or unknown pair with ACCESS_NOT_CANONICAL (cause = the contract's AccessParseError) and returns the contract-parsed pair; the parser is the package export @empressaio/atom-contract/access parseAccessPair (available in 1.30.0, no shim needed).
design.producers: conformant.mjs 153/173/509 -> PUBLIC_RECORD_ACCESS; flood.mjs floodAtomsToStage -> PUBLIC_RECORD_ACCESS; adapt/cad.mjs candidate access -> PUBLIC_RECORD_ACCESS (one producer constant in the repo; a divergence test ties it to the contract's mapAccessPolicy(public-free)).
design.boundary: assertNewShapeBoundary validates row.access after the node/key/DID checks; copyStage validates every atom before its INSERT; accessPolicyProjection refuses a legacy pair (ACCESS_NOT_CANONICAL) and keeps the canonical projection; sixFieldCandidate refuses a legacy pair.
design.restampJob: src/jobs/restamp-access.mjs runRestampAccess(env, {flags, deps}): flags --county (required, TX-validated), --apply | --dry-run (one required), --batch-size (default 5000), --run-id; --apply refuses LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN unless FACTORY_CLOUD=1 before any connect; ATOMS_DATABASE_URL required, pooler refused, current_database() must be hauska_mcp (WRONG_DATABASE); run row first (phase restamp-access, scope.command restamp-access, max_duration_s 7200, legacy table keys and canonical pair recorded in scope); per county: count legacy rows per (entity_type, legacy key) from the store, count rows whose access_policy disagrees with the table's policy (refuse ACCESS_COLUMN_DISAGREES), count out-of-table and canonical rows (reported, never touched); zero matched refuses RESTAMP_NOTHING_MATCHED (a run that writes nothing cannot succeed); for each entity type with matches: Factory scoped lease (entity_type, county) + lock, then keyset batches on atom_did, each batch one transaction: atoms_writer_lease_v2 take on <entity_type>:<county> (LEASE_HELD refuses), SELECT dids where legacy predicate, UPDATE body = body || {access: canonical, accessRestampedFrom: <legacy pair>, accessRestampRunId, accessRestampedAt}, access_policy = table policy WHERE atom_did = ANY(dids) AND the same legacy predicate; written must equal matched (RESTAMP_BATCH_SHORT), release lease, COMMIT, run_event restamp-batch {entityType, legacyKey, batchIndex, matched, written, firstAtomDid, lastAtomDid}; after all types: read-back legacy count must be 0 (RESTAMP_INCOMPLETE) and rows carrying this run's accessRestampRunId must equal total written (RESTAMP_COUNT_MISMATCH); termination success 7200. Dry run: counts only, run_event restamp-dry-run, no lease, no UPDATE, then DRY_RUN_REFUSED with runs.status failed / refuse_code and termination exit_kind dry-run (the 831fec74 rule). Every failure path writes runs.refuse_code and a termination.

If grep -rn '"public"' src finds a producer outside src/lib/access-pair.mjs, item 1's check fails.
